markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged Orbit the Sun readings for Madrid (a June/summer-solstice reading and a December/winter-solstice reading, with their different daylight hours) as evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine date/daylight-hours pairs from the student's own Investigation Record rows (about 14.9 h in June and about 9.1 h in December for Madrid with real tilt); exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('summer days are longer') with no actual logged readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains the mechanism: Earth's axis is tilted (about 23.5 degrees), so in June the Northern Hemisphere (Madrid) leans toward the Sun and gets more direct sunlight and longer days, while in December it leans away and gets shorter days.
markingScheme.accept: Any valid phrasing of axis tilt leading to leaning toward/away from the Sun; the number 23.5 is not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'because of the seasons' or 'because it is summer' with no mention of tilt or leaning toward/away from the Sun.

markingScheme.criterion: States that Earth's distance from the Sun is NOT the reason, with a reason (for example: Earth's orbit is almost a circle so the distance barely changes, or the no-tilt test showed 12 hours of daylight all year even though Earth still orbited the Sun).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that distance does not cause the seasons together with a supporting reason or a reference to the student's own no-tilt reading.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'it is not the distance' with no reason.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies the error: the seasons are caused by the tilt of Earth's axis, not by Earth being nearer to or farther from the Sun (Earth is in fact closest to the Sun in the Northern Hemisphere's winter).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that tilt, not distance, causes seasons.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'your friend is wrong' with no reason.

markingScheme.criterion: States that Australia (Southern Hemisphere) is having SUMMER when Madrid has winter - the seasons are opposite in the two hemispheres.
markingScheme.accept: Summer / warm season / opposite season; any clear statement that Australia has the opposite season to Spain.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying Australia also has winter, or giving no season.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why: when the Northern Hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun the Southern Hemisphere is tilted toward it, so Australia gets more direct sunlight and longer days.
markingScheme.accept: Any valid phrasing that the two halves lean opposite ways, so one gets more direct sunlight while the other gets less.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating that the seasons are opposite with no mention of tilting toward or away from the Sun.
